rv.q: For four decades, Jesse Malin was the music mayor of New York’s East Village. Beginning in the early ‘80s with his teenaged hardcore band Heart Attack through his years with the rock band D-Generation, his solo career and his Coney Island High nightclub, he was never a superstar but was a well-known, well-connected and tireless booster for the...
Silver Manhattan is a smart business move, documentation of Malin's hard-fought journey, and a very solid rock set.
This is Holy water for your soul!
If it’s your kind of theater, it’s a kick—possibly offering one of the best nights many have spent in a theater.

But this is a powerful work that belongs to a lineage of serious, meritorious rock musicals, such as The Lieutenant, the unjustly forgotten My Lai–inspired work that garnered multiple Tony and Drama Desk nominations in 1975.

cn.t: Critics praise Jesse Malin's Silver Manhattan as a powerful rock-theater hybrid that transcends the jukebox musical format, with most calling it a transformative and soul-stirring experience that showcases both his musical talent and personal resilience.
